newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INDIA ISSUES SIX-MONTH TERM KERO BUY TENDER.
newsitem.headline: INDIA ISSUES SIX-MONTH TERM KERO BUY TENDER.

text.p: State owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued a term tender to buy superior kerosene (SKO) for six months starting October 1997, traders said on Tuesday.
The tender is for 40,000-45,000 tonnes of SKO to be delivered in the second decade of each month to Kandla on the Indian east coast.
It closes on August 28 and is valid until September 1.
IOC issued a one-year term tender in March to buy SKO, but decided not to make any award.

Earlier this month IOC renewed its evergreen term purchase contract to buy 1.08 million tonnes of SKO from Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) for April 1997-March 1998 delivery at a 22-cent premium to MidEast spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.
It's previous contract with KPC was for the delivery of 1.0 million tonnes at 52 cents premium.

IOC also has similar term contracts with other national oil companies in the Middle East, including Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) and Bahrain National Oil Co (BANOCO) for about 540,000 tonnes annually.
In addtion, IOC has a one-year term tender with KPC for the delivery of one 30,000-tonne cargoe each per month to the east and west coast, traders said.
